rmt-2012-geo-08.title: Johnson's circles
rmt-2012-geo-08.body:
Let $X$ be the common point of the three circles. Then $O_aX=O_bX=O_cX=r$, and $X$ is the circumcenter of $O_aO_bO_c$. Also $AO_bXO_c$, $BO_cXO_a$, $CO_aXO_b$ are rhombi (all sides $r$). From the rhombi, $AO_b\parallel XO_c\parallel BO_a$ with $AO_b=BO_a=r$, so $ABO_aO_b$ is a parallelogram and $O_aO_b=AB$; likewise $O_bO_c=BC$ and $O_cO_a=CA$. So $O_aO_bO_c$ is congruent to $ABC$ and $r$ is its circumradius, equal to the circumradius of $ABC$: $R=\frac{abc}{4[ABC]}$. Here $s=7$ and $[ABC]=\sqrt{7\cdot4\cdot2\cdot1}=2\sqrt{14}$, so $R=\frac{3\cdot5\cdot6}{8\sqrt{14}}=\frac{45}{4\sqrt{14}}=\frac{45\sqrt{14}}{56}$.

**Answer: $\frac{45\sqrt{14}}{56}$**
